items.title: Chris Parker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 5, 2023
items.q: And my side is with a great bass player Anthony Jackson and we had worked together a lot. And Joe Beck on guitar and Bobby Scott on piano.

ctx.x: Yeah, you were way down the line, I know.

In each case it’s kind of different. Let’s see, Lionel Hampton was a date that Teo Macero produced and I had worked with Teo Macero on a Gato Barbieri record and he didn’t scare me. He was always kind of tempestuous you know, he had a temper and his face would get red and he would yell — I saw him yell at people you know who missed an eighth note in the second bar or something. But I wasn’t fazed by him on that — that’s the only thing I can think of, and I got a call for this Lionel Hampton date and I was…

bunch of different groups. But there’s only, at that time there was only so many places to play in Woodstock and I always noticed this guy standing in the background with a fur hat, big fur hat, you could only see his face and he had this giant like an Eskimo fur hat on. And I thought you know it was a typical character in Woodstock, I had no idea it was Paul Butterfield and he had been checking me out in all these different contexts and then one day I got a call from him and I said, “Yeah, right” and I hung up.…
